title: QBR: Onyx Systems - Health & Usage Review
summary: Quarterly business review covering onboarding/usage growth, rising token costs, recent reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Action items: send pricing breakouts, run latency benchmark on dedicated pool, share SOC2 + KMS docs. Agreed follow-up demo for dedicated configuration and cost model.
next_steps: Jordan to send updated usage-based pricing breakdown by 2026-01-20
Maya to schedule dedicated-pool perf run (1k concurrent requests) week of 2026-01-26
Samir to share SOC2 report and KMS integration guide by 2026-01-19
Customer to provide decision timeline for Dedicated pilot by 2026-02-05
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send cost breakdown and recommended batching/quantization profile - due 2026-01-20
Maya Chen: Run dedicated pool benchmark and share logs - due 2026-02-02
Samir Patel: Share SOC2 + KMS docs and audit log samples - due 2026-01-19
Ravi Kumar: Share 3 example prompt sets for regression monitoring - due 2026-01-22
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR. We have about 45 minutes, agenda is usage, costs, reliability items, and roadmap alignment. Samir and Maya from our side, and from Onyx we have Ravi, Elena, Marcus - thanks for being here.
[00:18] Elena Soto: Thanks Jordan, excited to get through this. We've seen a lot of adoption since last quarter.
[00:24] Samir Patel: Quick note — I'll cover ops and alerts; Maya will go deep on perf when we hit that section.
[00:30] Ravi Kumar: Great. High level: usage is up about 3x since October, a bunch of chat features and embeddings for search. Costs, though, are starting to surprise our finance team.
[00:42] Jordan Lee: Yep, we expected growth. We pulled numbers: your average token spend grew from ~120k tokens/day to ~360k tokens/day, and the majority of that is generation for customer-facing chat flows. That's where batching and KV cache could save you 20-40% by prefix caching.
[01:05] Marcus Li: To add, our SREs saw spikes in P95 latency last month — there were two incidents where tail latency jumped to ~900ms for about 30 minutes. We tracked them to a model fallback event.
[01:20] Maya Chen: Right, that's the routing fallback kicking in when your primary variant hit capacity. We recommended a reserved burst policy and compatible fallback variant — that reduces tail significantly. In internal tests, p95 dropped from 420ms to 280ms with canary + reserved burst.
[01:40] Ravi Kumar: Okay, what does that mean cost-wise? If we add reserved capacity, will our unit cost go up? Finance is nervous about committing.
[01:49] Jordan Lee: Good question. There are tradeoffs: hosted on pay-as-you-go gives no commit but higher per-token unit cost at heavy volume. Dedicated/reserved capacity lowers per-token cost but requires a commit. For your current volume, a small Dedicated pool with autoscale can lower cost by roughly 18-28% depending on utilization. We'll send a modeled breakdown based on your last 90 days.
[02:12] Elena Soto: We need the breakdown by team and by route. Can you show us where the costs are coming from?
[02:18] Jordan Lee: We'll export route-level token metrics and add recommended batching config per route. Also include impact of quantization — 8-bit quantized variants can reduce GPU runtime and cost but we need to validate quality on your prompts.
[02:31] Samir Patel: On security, you asked about audit logs and KMS. We're SOC 2 Type II and we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. I'll share the SOC2 report and the KMS integration guide after the call.
[02:45] Marcus Li: For private deployments, latency improves but there's more ops overhead — is Redwood's private option fully supported?
[02:51] Maya Chen: Yes — Private gives you a control plane in your VPC or on-prem package; it supports RBAC, SAML SSO, and audit logs. It also allows you to pin model versions and use your own KMS. We can scope a pilot if you want.
[03:06] Ravi Kumar: Let's talk reliability incidents. Two incidents last month — what's the root cause and what are we changing?
[03:13] Maya Chen: Root cause was a transient throttling event plus a model variant mismatch during a rollout. Fixes: implement automatic canary rollouts for model changes, increase KV cache size for hot prefixes, and tune routing policies to prefer lower-latency regions. We've proposed config changes in the shared doc.
[03:31] Elena Soto: Who will run those changes — us or Redwood?
[03:35] Jordan Lee: We can push the configuration as part of a managed change during the pilot; for Private, you'll run with our ops assistance. We'll include step-by-step notes.
[03:44] Marcus Li: For the dedicated pilot, what SLA can we expect?
[03:47] Jordan Lee: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we can commit to a 99.9% uptime SLA for the pool and define p95 latency SLOs in the pilot. Exact SLOs depend on the model and sequence-length distributions.
[04:03] Ravi Kumar: Can you run a bench with our real prompt sets? That's the most important.
[04:07] Maya Chen: Absolutely — we asked for three representative prompt sets. Once we have them, we'll run a 1k concurrent request benchmark on a dedicated pool and return logs, cost per 1M tokens, and tail-latency breakdown.
[04:19] Jordan Lee: Action items: we'll send the cost model, SOC2/KMS docs, and schedule the perf run. On the roadmap piece, any features you want prioritized?
[04:28] Elena Soto: Better routing visibility — we sometimes don't know when a request fell back to another region or model. An automatic trace linking token counts to route decisions would help.
[04:37] Samir Patel: We actually have a tracing hook planned — per-route tracing with decision metadata; we'll try to surface that in the console beta. I'll put you on the beta list.
[04:47] Ravi Kumar: Also, alerting. We want earlier alerts for rising error rates rather than after an incident.
[04:53] Maya Chen: We can add a rule set: alert at 0.2% error rate sustained for 5 minutes at route-level. We'll propose thresholds in the follow-up doc.
[05:03] Jordan Lee: Any concerns about data residency or compliance?
[05:07] Elena Soto: We're subject to EU data residency for a segment of customers. Can Redwood route and store embeddings in eu-west region only?
[05:15] Samir Patel: Yes — we support region pinning and separate model catalogs by region. We'll document how to set up route-level region pins and encryption-at-rest keys per region.
[05:25] Marcus Li: One more — monitoring noise. We keep getting duplicate alerts for the same root cause. Can we consolidate?
[05:30] Maya Chen: We'll propose an alert aggregation rule and correlate by incident ID. That should cut noise significantly.
[05:38] Jordan Lee: Great. Recap of next steps: Jordan sends cost model and batching recs; Samir sends SOC2 + KMS docs and adds Onyx to tracing beta; Maya schedules dedicated perf benchmark after Ravi shares prompt sets; Onyx provides decision timeline for pilot.
[05:56] Ravi Kumar: Sounds good. Timeline — we aim to decide on pilot by the first week of February.
[06:02] Elena Soto: We'll circulate internal stakeholder notes and get you a timeline.
[06:06] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the docs and links to the shared benchmark sheet.
[06:12] (meeting ends)
